paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God's wonders are meant to be passed down and never forgotten. Asaph says the fathers were to teach their children so the coming generation would "put their confidence in God, not forgetting His works, but keeping His commandments." (Psalm 78:7) Forgetting is where the trouble starts, and I know a little about being shoved in the back and forgotten, so I'm telling you, this one matters.

Now look at how forgetting plays out. The people saw the sea split and water come out of a rock, and still they asked, "Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?" (Psalm 78:19) The text says they "did not believe God or rely on His salvation." (Psalm 78:22) So here's a question to carry around, baker: what has God already done for you that you keep skipping over when the next worry shows up? That's the whole lesson in one oven mitt.

And here's the part that gets me every time. Even when their hearts were disloyal, "He was compassionate; He forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them." (Psalm 78:38) Then Asaph says, "He remembered that they were but flesh, a passing breeze that does not return." (Psalm 78:39) God doesn't forget us, even when we forget Him, so remember His works, tell them to somebody, and keep trusting Him. Asaph is not done with this story, friend, so stay close.
